title.en: Sufia Kamal · Poetry, shelter and women’s public voice
title.zh: 苏菲娅·卡迈勒 · 诗歌、庇护与女性公共声音

location.label: Dhaka; representative literary and civic organizing context

summary.en:
Sufia Kamal made literary work and public organizing part of the same life. Born in 1911 in Shayestabad near Barisal, she received education at home, learning Bangla from family alongside other languages. Her access to print developed through editors and writers rather than a conventional university career. Her poem Basanti appeared in 1926, and her collection Sanjher Maya followed in 1938. These publications brought a woman’s voice into a literary world in which access to education and public authority remained unequal.

Widowed while young, she remained in Kolkata with her family and taught in a municipal girls’ school from 1933 to 1941. During communal violence in 1946 she helped establish shelter for victims at Lady Brabourne College. In 1947 she became the first editor of the women’s weekly Begum; later that year her family moved to Dhaka. Writing, teaching and practical relief were interconnected forms of work, rather than successive replacements for one another.

She participated in the 1952 Bengali language movement and opposed restrictions on Bengali cultural expression. Bangladesh Mahila Parishad’s own account dates its establishment through her initiative to 1970, after the organizing climate of 1969. During the 1971 liberation war she kept diaries recording violence and resistance. She continued cultural and women’s organizing after independence and died in Dhaka in 1999. Her story connects literature to the institutions that made women’s participation possible without treating one celebrated author as the whole movement.
summary.zh:
苏菲娅·卡迈勒把文学创作与公共组织工作融为一体。她1911年出生于巴里萨尔附近的沙耶斯塔巴德，在家中受教，除其他语言外，也向亲人学习孟加拉语。她进入出版界的道路依靠编辑和作家网络，而非通常的大学生涯。1926年发表诗作《春日》，1938年出版诗集《暮色的魅力》。在教育与公共权威分配不平等的环境里，这些作品使女性声音进入文坛。

年轻守寡后，她与家人留在加尔各答，1933至1941年在市立女子小学任教。1946年宗教群体暴力发生时，她协助在布拉伯恩夫人学院为受害者建立庇护场所。1947年担任女性周刊《贝古姆》首任编辑，同年稍后随家迁往达卡。写作、教学与实际救助并非相互替代的阶段，而是彼此联系的工作。

她参加1952年孟加拉语运动，反对压制孟加拉文化。孟加拉国妇女理事会自身的记载将其在她倡议下正式成立的时间定为1970年，背景是1969年的组织动员。1971年解放战争期间，她用日记记录暴力与抵抗。独立后继续文化和妇女组织工作，1999年在达卡去世。其生平把文学与促成女性公共参与的机构联系起来，但不能用一位名作家替代整个运动。

title.en: Mahila Parishad · From public demands to practical support
title.zh: 妇女理事会 · 从公共诉求到实际支持

location.label: Dhaka; representative literary and civic organizing context

summary.en:
Bangladesh Mahila Parishad emerged from women’s organizing amid the mass mobilization of late 1960s East Pakistan. Its institutional history dates the association’s beginning to April 1970, with Sufia Kamal among its founders. Its subsequent name reflected the creation of Bangladesh in 1971. The organization connected demands for political equality with the everyday conditions that limited women’s ability to exercise rights.

Its early work included a 1971 publication documenting wartime violence against Bengali women. In 1972 activists pressed for changes concerning inheritance, parliamentary representation and girls’ education. An anti-dowry signature campaign in 1976–1977 brought household relations into public debate. Advocacy formed part of a wider political process; the account does not establish that one organization alone caused later legislation.

Rokeya Sadan, established in 1984, added shelter and support for women and girls facing violence. Legal assistance, education and livelihood work linked public campaigning with practical needs. The chosen interval follows these early institutional developments, not the end of the organization. Its stated democratic and non-communal commitments describe aims; they do not prove that equality was achieved or that every woman shared the same experience.
summary.zh:
孟加拉国妇女理事会产生于东巴基斯坦1960年代末群众动员背景下的女性组织活动。机构史将其起点定于1970年4月，苏菲娅·卡迈勒是发起者之一。1971年孟加拉国建立后，组织采用与新国家相应的名称。它把政治平等诉求与妨碍女性实际行使权利的日常条件联系起来。

早期活动包括1971年出版记录孟加拉女性战争受害经历的资料。1972年，活动者提出继承、议会代表和女童教育方面的改革要求。1976至1977年的反嫁妆签名运动，使家庭关系进入公共讨论。倡议是更广泛政治过程的一部分，现有叙述不能证明后来立法完全由单一组织促成。

1984年建立的罗凯娅庇护所为面临暴力的妇女和女童提供住所及支持。法律援助、教育与谋生活动，把公共运动同具体需求连接起来。所选时间段追踪早期机构发展，并非组织活动的终点。它所宣示的民主与非宗派承诺代表目标，不能证明平等已经实现，也不能代替每位女性各不相同的经历。

dateNote.en: 1970–1984 follows establishment through the early shelter initiative. The organization continued afterward; the older reference entry’s membership figures are not presented as current.
dateNote.zh: 1970—1984年追踪成立至早期庇护项目。组织此后持续活动，不把旧参考条目的会员数当作现状。

title.en: Ananda Coomaraswamy · From field survey to the art museum
title.zh: 阿南达·库马拉斯瓦米 · 从实地调查到艺术博物馆

location.label: Colombo; birthplace and representative Ceylon institutional context

summary.en:
Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy built a career across scientific survey, craft documentation and the study of South Asian art. Born in Colombo in 1877 to a Ceylonese father and an English mother, he grew up largely in Britain. He studied at University College London and graduated in 1900. Work for Ceylon’s Mineralogical Survey from 1903 to 1906 returned him to the island through a scientific institution rather than an art-school appointment.

During those years Ananda and his wife Ethel documented objects and makers in photographs and drawings. Their albums record weaving, ceramics, metalwork, woodwork and other practices, with a strong emphasis on Kandyan districts. Ethel’s contribution is part of the archive’s authorship, not merely an accompaniment to her husband’s career. The material fed into his 1908 book Mediaeval Sinhalese Art, which linked descriptions of objects with questions about craftspeople and social organization.

In 1910 he helped establish the India Society in London to promote Indian art. In 1917 he took a museum research appointment in Boston, where he worked until 1947. His movement between survey offices, learned societies and collections shows how knowledge depended on institutions as well as an individual scholar. The surviving albums also leave questions: whose labour was named, which places were selected and what changed when objects became museum examples? He died in 1947. His biography introduces those questions without treating his interpretations as the final account of Sri Lankan or Indian artistic life.
summary.zh:
阿南达·肯蒂什·库马拉斯瓦米的职业横跨科学调查、工艺记录与南亚艺术研究。他1877年生于科伦坡，父亲来自锡兰，母亲是英国人，主要在英国长大。1900年从伦敦大学学院毕业。1903至1906年，他在锡兰矿物调查机构工作，通过科学机构而非艺术院校的职位回到岛上。

这段时期，他与妻子埃塞尔用照片和图画记录器物及制作者。相册涉及编织、陶器、金属、木作等工艺，重点在康提地区。埃塞尔是档案的共同作者，不能仅被视为丈夫事业的陪伴者。相关材料进入他1908年的《中世纪僧伽罗艺术》，把器物描述与工匠及社会组织问题联系起来。

1910年，他参与在伦敦成立推广印度艺术的印度学会。1917年赴波士顿任博物馆研究职位，在那里工作至1947年。从调查机构、学术团体到收藏机构的经历，显示知识既依靠个人学者，也依靠制度。留存相册同时提出问题：谁的劳动得到署名，哪些地方被选择，器物成为博物馆范例后发生了什么变化？他1947年去世。其生平可引入这些问题，但不能把他的解释当作斯里兰卡或印度艺术生活的最终结论。

title.en: Ceylon craft albums · Makers, photographs and selective archives
title.zh: 锡兰工艺相册 · 制作者、摄影与选择性的档案

location.label: Kandy; representative regional emphasis of a dispersed documentation project

summary.en:
Between 1903 and 1906 Ananda and Ethel Coomaraswamy assembled photographic records of arts and crafts in Ceylon, now Sri Lanka. Four surviving albums identify both as authors. Images and drawings were organized largely by material and practice: weaving, ceramics, ivory, metal, wood and architecture. The collection includes artisans as well as objects, with a strong emphasis on Kandyan districts.

This was a selected record of a living craft world, not a comprehensive survey of an unchanging national tradition. Some objects were in Colombo or Kandy museums; many photographs were made during tours. The archival description also identifies Tamil pottery and jewellery and objects labelled Dutch. These distinctions resist reducing the island’s making practices to a single isolated style.

The albums supplied material for Ananda’s 1908 Mediaeval Sinhalese Art. Reading them alongside his career highlights Ethel’s contribution and the labour of the makers represented. The present entry uses the archive project’s description, not an independent attribution of every pictured object. Its dates refer to documentation and publication; they neither date the origins of the crafts nor imply that their makers’ traditions ended in 1908.
summary.zh:
1903至1906年间，阿南达与埃塞尔·库马拉斯瓦米在锡兰，即今日斯里兰卡，建立艺术和工艺的摄影记录。留存的四册相册将两人列为作者。照片和图画大致按材料与实践分类，包括编织、陶器、象牙、金属、木作和建筑。收藏既呈现器物，也呈现工匠，重点涉及康提地区。

这是一份对活跃工艺世界的选择性记录，并非对某种不变民族传统的全面普查。部分器物来自科伦坡或康提博物馆，许多照片摄于巡访途中。档案说明还指出泰米尔陶器和首饰，以及被标作荷兰的物品。这些区别提醒读者，不能把岛上的制作实践化约为单一封闭风格。

相册为阿南达1908年的《中世纪僧伽罗艺术》提供材料。与他的生平并读，可以看见埃塞尔的贡献及被记录制作者的劳动。本条采用档案项目说明，并非独立鉴定每件器物。日期对应记录与出版，不是工艺的起源时间，也不意味着制作者的传统在1908年终结。

title.en: Hiratsuka Raichō · Writing women into public debate
title.zh: 平塚雷鸟 · 让女性进入公共论辩

location.label: Tokyo; representative educational and editorial setting

summary.en:
Hiratsuka Raichō used writing and organization to challenge the restricted place assigned to women in modern Japan. Born in Tokyo in 1886, she completed study at Japan Women’s University in 1906. Her interest in ideas beyond the expected domestic curriculum, alongside a sustained engagement with Zen practice, shaped a search for intellectual independence. This was one woman’s path within unequal educational arrangements, not evidence that all women experienced the same opportunities.

In 1911 she helped establish the Seitō-sha collective and launched the magazine Seitō. Its opening editorial called on women to recover their own creative authority. The journal began with literature and increasingly addressed social questions, relationships and control over women’s bodies. Editors and contributors made it a shared undertaking. Public criticism, school restrictions and seizure of issues show that publication did not guarantee secure access to public speech.

Her later activism moved into organizational politics. The National Diet Library dates the formation of the New Woman’s Association with Ichikawa Fusae to 1920. Hiratsuka advocated maternity protection while campaigning around women’s political participation. Different approaches to independence, work and motherhood remained subjects of debate rather than a single settled programme.

After the war she participated in peace and women’s movements. She died in 1971. Following her career from education through print to association-building connects individual expression with collective work; it also leaves room to ask which women were represented by the journals and institutions that survived.
summary.zh:
平塚雷鸟通过写作与组织活动，挑战近代日本给予女性的受限位置。她1886年生于东京，1906年从日本女子大学毕业。对家庭课程之外思想的兴趣，加上长期的禅修实践，推动了她对精神独立的探索。这是教育机会不平等背景下的个人道路，不能代表所有女性都有同样机遇。

1911年，她参与创立青鞜社并推出《青鞜》杂志。创刊辞呼吁女性恢复自身的创造权威。杂志起初以文学为中心，随后日益讨论社会问题、亲密关系以及对女性身体的控制。编辑和作者共同承担工作。公众批评、学校禁读及部分期刊被没收，说明获得出版机会并不意味着能够稳定地公开发言。

她后来进入组织政治。日本国立国会图书馆将她与市川房枝成立新妇人协会的时间记为1920年。她主张母性保护，也围绕女性政治参与开展活动。独立、劳动与母职之间的不同思路仍是争论对象，并未形成唯一确定的纲领。

战后，她参加和平及妇女运动，1971年去世。沿着教育、出版与协会建设的轨迹阅读其生平，可以把个人表达与集体工作联系起来；同时也需追问，留存的杂志和机构究竟代表了哪些女性。

dateNote.en: Lifespan 1886–1971. 1920 follows the National Diet Library’s formal-association chronology; the entry does not reconstruct earlier organizing meetings. Tokyo is a representative institutional setting.
dateNote.zh: 生卒1886—1971年。1920年采用国立国会图书馆的正式协会时间线，不重建更早的筹备会议。东京为代表性机构地点。

title.en: Seitō · A collective makes a literary public
title.zh: 《青鞜》 · 集体出版与文学公共空间

location.label: Tokyo; representative educational and editorial setting

summary.en:
Seitō’s first issue appeared on 1 September 1911. The women who edited and published it included Hiratsuka Raichō, Yasumochi Yoshiko, Mozume Kazuko, Kiuchi Teiko and Nakano Hatsuko. Treating the magazine as a collective makes visible the work behind a manifesto: selecting writing, assembling issues and creating a readership for women’s words.

Literary work became a means of discussing social authority. The magazine broadened its attention to relationships, sexuality and women’s autonomy, while translations brought writers from outside Japan into local debate. These connections did not erase differences among contributors or turn the magazine into the voice of every Japanese woman. Access depended on literacy, circulation and the ability to withstand public criticism.

Schools prohibited reading it, and authorities seized some issues as threats to public morals. Those responses show how the regulation of print could constrain a new discussion space. The selected early-years window is editorial, rather than a claim that the journal closed in 1915. This record follows the production and reception of a publication alongside Hiratsuka’s life, inviting comparison with education and other women’s writing already represented in the atlas.
summary.zh:
《青鞜》创刊号于1911年9月1日出版。参与编辑和发行的女性包括平塚雷鸟、保持研子、物集和子、木内锭子与中野初子。把杂志视为集体事业，就能看到宣言背后的工作：选择作品、编排期刊，并为女性文字建立读者群。

文学由此成为讨论社会权威的途径。杂志逐渐关注亲密关系、性及女性自主，通过翻译把日本以外的作者引入本地讨论。这些联系并未消除作者之间的分歧，也不使杂志自动成为所有日本女性的声音。阅读机会取决于识字、流通及承受社会批评的能力。

一些学校禁止学生阅读，当局也以有碍公共道德为由没收部分期刊。这些反应显示，出版管制会约束新出现的讨论空间。所选早期年份是编辑观察窗口，并非声称杂志于1915年停刊。本条将出版物的制作与接受过程同平塚的生平并读，并与图谱已有的教育及女性写作条目进行比较。

dateNote.en: 1911–1915 is a selected early-years focus, not the complete publication lifespan or an exact closure date. The inspected library account supports themes and reception; individual seized issues were not independently collated.
dateNote.zh: 1911—1915年是选择的早期观察段，并非完整刊期或确切停刊时间。所查图书馆说明支持主题与接受史，未独立核对每期被没收刊物。

title.en: Siti Walidah · Teaching, faith and women’s organization
title.zh: 西蒂·瓦利达 · 教学、信仰与妇女组织

location.label: Kauman, Yogyakarta; representative teaching and organizing neighbourhood

summary.en:
Siti Walidah, also known as Nyai Ahmad Dahlan, developed women’s education through religious learning and organization in Yogyakarta. Born in Kauman in 1872, she was educated at home and became a teacher in her family’s religious setting. Her 1889 marriage to the future founder of Muhammadiyah placed her within a reforming network, but her work also depended on relationships with girls, women workers and other teachers.

In 1914 she helped develop Sopo Tresno, a women’s learning circle. Teaching included religious interpretation and the importance of education. Aisyiyah’s account also describes literacy instruction for women employed in Kauman’s batik workshops after their working day. The timing mattered: access to learning had to fit around paid labour and household demands, rather than assuming that every student could attend a conventional school.

The formal Aisyiyah association emerged in 1917. Siti Bariyah was its first chair; Walidah’s role in nurturing the movement did not make her its first officeholder. Walidah was elected chair in 1921 and continued organizing after Ahmad Dahlan’s death in 1923. Girls’ schooling, hostels and religious instruction provided several ways to prepare women for public responsibility.

She remained associated with the movement until her death in Yogyakarta in 1946. Institutional biographies remember a model of religious commitment and service. Reading them critically keeps collective leadership and ordinary learners in view, while avoiding the claim that one person or one organization completed the work of women’s emancipation.
summary.zh:
西蒂·瓦利达，又称妮艾·艾哈迈德·达赫兰，在日惹通过宗教学习与组织活动发展女性教育。她1872年出生于高曼社区，在家受教，后来在家庭宗教环境中任教。1889年，她嫁给后来创立穆罕默迪亚的达赫兰，进入改革网络；但她的工作也依靠同女孩、女工及其他教师建立的关系。

1914年，她协助发展妇女学习团体“相互关爱”。教学涉及宗教解释及教育的重要性。阿伊莎组织的记载还描述，她在高曼蜡染作坊女工下班后提供识字和宗教教学。时间安排很关键：学习机会必须适应有酬劳动和家庭责任，不能假设所有学生都能进入常规学校。

阿伊莎于1917年成为正式协会。首任主席是西蒂·巴里娅；瓦利达培育运动的作用并不意味着她是第一任负责人。她1921年当选主席，达赫兰1923年去世后仍继续组织工作。女子学校、宿舍与宗教教学，为女性承担公共责任提供多种路径。

她持续与运动相联系，1946年在日惹去世。机构传记将其记为宗教承诺与服务的典范。批判性阅读这些材料，需要保留集体领导和普通学习者的位置，避免声称一人或一个组织已经完成女性解放。

dateNote.en: Lifespan 1872–1946. Dates identify the learning circle, formal association and chairmanship separately. Kauman is a neighbourhood reference, not a precise classroom. Conflicting preschool dates are omitted.
dateNote.zh: 生卒1872—1946年。分别标示学习团体、正式协会与主席任职的时间。高曼为社区参考点，不是精确教室。相互冲突的幼儿园日期未采用。

title.en: Aisyiyah · Study circles become an educational network
title.zh: 阿伊莎 · 从学习圈到教育网络

location.label: Kauman, Yogyakarta; representative teaching and organizing neighbourhood

summary.en:
The beginnings of Aisyiyah show how an educational movement could grow from neighbourhood relationships. A 1914 women’s study circle in Kauman preceded the formal association established in 1917. Meetings, religious interpretation and literacy work created opportunities for women to teach and organize within the Muhammadiyah network.

Leadership was collective. Siti Bariyah became the first chair, with women filling secretarial, treasury and supporting roles; Siti Walidah acted as an important teacher and guide before later chairing the association. This distinction matters because a history centred only on a founder’s household can obscure the younger organizers who operated the institution.

Girls’ schooling, hostels and instruction for working women linked learning to practical schedules and community life. The organization also developed early-childhood education, although its own webpages disagree on the first preschool’s year, so no precise founding date is used here. Suara Aisyiyah, launched in 1926, added an organizational magazine through which ideas could circulate beyond a meeting room. The chosen interval follows these early forms of association, teaching and print. It does not imply that educational opportunity became universal or that the network ended in 1926.
summary.zh:
阿伊莎的开端显示，教育运动如何从社区关系中成长。高曼1914年的妇女学习团体先于1917年成立的正式协会。聚会、宗教解释及识字工作，为女性在穆罕默迪亚网络内教学和组织提供机会。

领导工作是集体承担的。西蒂·巴里娅成为首任主席，其他女性担任秘书、财务及辅助职务；西蒂·瓦利达先作为重要教师和指导者，后来才出任主席。这个区别很重要：若历史只围绕创办者家庭，就可能遮蔽实际运作机构的年轻组织者。

女子学校、宿舍及面向女工的教学，把学习与实际作息和社区生活联系起来。组织也开展幼儿教育，但自身网页对首所幼儿园的年份存在分歧，因此此处不采用精确创办日期。1926年创办的《阿伊莎之声》增加了组织刊物，使思想能够走出会议场所流通。所选时间段追踪早期的协会、教学与出版形式，并不意味着教育机会已普及，也不表示网络在1926年结束。

dateNote.en: 1914–1926 links the precursor circle, 1917 formal association and 1926 magazine. The institutional profile gives 1919 for Frobel School, while its Walidah biography gives 1922; this unresolved disagreement is not converted into a milestone.
dateNote.zh: 1914—1926年连接前身团体、1917年正式协会及1926年杂志。机构简介将福禄贝尔学校定于1919年，而瓦利达传记给出1922年；未解决的分歧不转为生平节点。
